As in the original Terra Mystica, fourteen different factions live on seven different kinds of planets, and each faction is bound to their own home planets, so to develop and grow, they must terraform neighboring planets into their home environments in competition with the other groups. In addition, Gaia planets can be used by all factions for colonization, and Transdimensional planets can be changed into Gaia planets. All factions can improve their skills in six different areas of development — Terraforming, Navigation, Artificial Intelligence, Gaiaforming, Economy, Research — leading to advanced technology and special bonuses. To do all of that, each group has special skills and abilities. Number of players: 1 - 4 Game duration: 66 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Gaia Project and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. [Rating: 1/10] Much better game than Terra Mystica, but not enough better to win me over.  2018-08-29: (reducing from 5.5) I've had an epiphany.  Terra Mystica is Catan 2.0 and Gaia Project is Catan 2.5.  The primary mechanism in all 3 is building up connected settlements.  Also, in all 3, the state of the game after the players place their first buildings is the single largest factor in the outcome of the game - which is why they are horrible games unworthy of anybodies time or interest.

[Rating: 1/10] Bad component quality, extra rules with respect to TM without adding any depth, unbalanced races, complete waste of money, stick to TM.

[Rating: 1/10] I can't get behind any game that is a re-implementation of Terra Mystica, even if it has an awesome space theme to it.. Still the same shitty Terra Mystica underneath..

[Rating: 1/10] This is just the reimplementation of a puzzle game.  Learn the puzzle.  Win the Game.  Repeat.  Boring.

[Rating: 1/10] Terra Mystica in Space. Much prefer the Mk1 version TM and the additional rules relating to technology and the Gaia Project simply make the game worse. - Missing the tension of the Terra Mystica land grab - Factions have less theme than TM - Tech tree symbology is a lot to process - Much longer than TM, over 4+ hours with 3p, which lowers the decision density to tedium

[Rating: 1/10] The brain rapist. Another BGG top 100 game about nothing. It represents the genre „Let’s put into the game as many abstract and counterintuitive elements and mechanisms as only possible and let’s pretend that all this fits well together in way that only elite geeks can appreciate”. Don’t get fooled with colorful boards, plenty of beatiful elements an other stuff. The game is bloody heavy in the worst, non elegant way. Unlike Lacerda’s games - another master of this genre - here I didn’t find even tiny element or mechanism that would be interesting, attractive or innovative.

[Rating: 1/10] The most long, boring and drawn out awful experience I've ever had playing this game the three times I had to.   I played with experts at this game and the only thing I can say is, if you don't study every strategy, opening and faction you are basically a useless bot waiting for your turn. Downtime is a lot, the interaction is minimal, you are playing a solo game when sometimes you have to rethink what to do next.
